decision.changed_angle: The prior April2 basket overlaps in three names, but the Tesla lead now addresses newly eligible April2 completed delivery decline and its quoted stock reaction. Reuters n1020 and CNBC n1021 replace the earlier pending/recovery framing with actual customer-demand evidence; n0910 complicates the apparent regained sales ranking. This is a changed operating test, not a price-only retitle or a popularity inference.

Tesla is frequent in the preceding editions, but April5-6 brings a newly announced August8 robotaxi unveiling and an explicitly disputed low-cost-car report. The lead changes from completed delivery/analyst-target issues to competing strategic routes and a pending milestone. Reuters report and Musk denial stay side by side; the unveiling is not treated as a commercial launch. Newly eligible cited evidence supports retaining this substantive change despite concentration.

Tesla is secondary after the April8 full strategy lead. New April8 Barrons n1083 expressly links the stock jump to the robotaxi plan; the item distinguishes this completed market response from the prior announcement and from a completed commercial service. The investment test now asks whether the reaction persists while low-cost-car disagreement remains unresolved. This is a newly evidenced reaction, not an unchanged full lead or fabricated retail flow.

The immediately prior April23 full lead explicitly carried diehard-holder commitment into a pending earnings result. Newly eligible April23 completed revenue/profit setbacks (Guardian n1391 and NPR n1389), accelerated more-affordable vehicle programme (Reuters n1095 and Axios n1390) and actual earnings-call technology/autonomy framing (Fortune n1379) now require owners to reconcile a reported weak quarter with a changed commercial promise. The current regular-session price is expressly an entry reference, not an earnings reaction. This is a substantive result-and-strategy update despite four appearances in five editions; it neither repeats the prior pending profile nor asserts completed demand recovery. Removed late n2168 contributes nothing to this decision.
